title: ヒューマンインタフェース設計学
subtitle: Designing of Human Interface
keywords: Human Interface 2.User Experience (UX) 3.Cognitive Property 4.Human Error 5.Regional Collaboration
educationalGoal: “Human Interface” refers to a system’s interface that humans can actually see and touch. If the interface is not user-friendly and has a lot of functions, we might fail to operate the system and it could cause problems or accidents. This lecture teaches knowledge of cognitive and physiological properties of the user, concepts of user experience (UX), and definitions of human centered design (HCD) in order to make the human interface more user-friendly.
advice: Topics covered in this lecture are as follows: 1. Basics of human interface. 2. UX and HCD process. 3. Cognitive properties and usability design. 4. Feedback and temporal elements in human interface. 5. Human error. Special lectures on designing the interface by product development experts in private enterprises are going to be planned.
books: Textbooks:None Reference books:User experience design textbook (Maruzen Publishing), An illustrated guide to human interface 2nd ed. (Kodansha) Reserved books:None
requiredKnowledge: UX design is an issue in daily life, and you must be always aware of the usability of products around you. Talking, recording and taking pictures without permission during the lecture are prohibited. Seats are assigned every time.

activityGoals.body: Ability to understand and explain the roles of human interface.
Ability to understand and explain user experience.
Ability to understand and explain the human-centered design process.
Ability to understand and explain the importance of appropriate feedback to users.
Ability to understand and explain the cause and solution of human error.

achievementLevels.ideal: Ability to apply ergonomic design technology in order to design a more user-friendly experience. Ability to propose useful interface design in familiar daily products.
achievementLevels.standard: Ability to explain human interface and human-centered design. Ability to explain an example of useful design in which human property is considered in familiar daily products.

lessons.content: Course introduction Basics of human interface (1)
lessons.assignments: Review: look for examples of human interface in daily life and think about their usability. Prep: search for studies on human interface conducted in companies.

Review: explain the interaction between humans and machines or tools in daily life with the man-machine system model, and analyze its user-friendliness and user-unfriendliness. Prep: read the chapter on human-centered design in ISO and JIS.

lessons.content: User experience (UX) and Human-Centered Design (HCD) process (1)
lessons.assignments: Review: think about usability of some devices in daily life. Prep: review human properties which you’ve learned in the other lectures.

lessons.content: User experience (UX) and Human-Centered Design (HCD) process (2)
lessons.assignments: Review: search for a company that has introduced human-centered design process. Prep: review what you've learned up to the 4th lecture and prepare for quiz (1).
Review: summarize what you learned and what you thought through special lecture (1). Prep: review what you've learned up to the 5th lecture and prepare for quiz (1).

lessons.content: Quiz (1) Cognitive properties and usability design (1)
lessons.assignments: Review: review quiz (1). Prep: examine the usability of an app you usually use.

lessons.content: Review of Quiz (1) Cognitive properties and usability design (2)
lessons.assignments: Review: review quiz (1). Prep: search for examples of interfaces that consider human properties.
Review: examine the usability of an app that you usually use. Prep: search for examples of feedback from devices in daily life.

Review: summarize what was discussed in the lecture, and consider the usability of devices used in daily life. Prep: investigate physical and psychological effects of feedback from a device on humans.

lessons.content: Feedback and temporal elements in human interface (2)
lessons.assignments: Review: check the timing of feedback when you use a device, and consider whether the timing is appropriate or not. Prep: summarize examples of how you failed to use devices in daily life.
Review: search for an accident caused by human error. Prep: review what you've learned up to the 11th lecture and prepare for quiz (2).
Review: summarize what you learned and what you thought through special lecture (2). Prep: review what you've learned up to the 13th lecture and prepare for quiz (2).
